sql_schemas: table employees | fields: id, employee_number, first_name, last_name, email, manager_id, department, hire_date, termination_date, employment_status, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at | pk: id | fks: manager_id -> employees.id | indexes: employee_number: unique lookup by employee number; email: unique lookup by email for auth and dedup; manager_id: team-level queries — find all direct reports of a manager; employment_status: filter active/inactive/terminated employees; department: department-scoped queries and reporting
table leave_types | fields: id, code, label, created_at | pk: id | indexes: code: unique lookup by leave type code (annual, sick, emergency, etc.)

table leave_policies | fields: id, policy_name, leave_type_id, entitlement_days, accrual_rate, max_accumulation, minimum_notice_days, requires_manager_approval, is_active, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: leave_type_id -> leave_types.id | indexes: leave_type_id: filter policies by leave type; is_active: filter active policies for rule evaluation; policy_name: lookup by policy name

table leave_requests | fields: id, employee_id, leave_type_id, start_date, end_date, reason, status, approved_by, approved_at, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id; leave_type_id -> leave_types.id; approved_by -> employees.id | indexes: employee_id: list all leave requests for an employee; balance deduction queries; status: filter by status (SUBMITTED for manager approval queues, APPROVED for calendar views); leave_type_id: filter requests by leave type; start_date: date-range queries for calendar views and overlap detection; end_date: date-range queries for calendar views and overlap detection; approved_by: find all requests approved by a specific manager

table leave_balances | fields: id, employee_id, policy_id, total_entitlement, used_days, remaining_days, fiscal_year, status, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id; policy_id -> leave_policies.id | indexes: employee_id: look up balances for a specific employee; policy_id: look up balances by policy; fiscal_year: filter balances by fiscal year for accrual and reset cycles; employee_id, policy_id, fiscal_year: unique constraint to prevent duplicate balance records per employee-policy-year

table audit_logs | fields: id, entity_type, entity_id, action, old_values, new_values, performed_by, performed_at, ip_address, user_agent, created_at | pk: id | fks: performed_by -> employees.id | indexes: entity_type, entity_id: look up all audit records for a specific entity (e.g. a leave request); performed_by: look up all actions by a specific user; performed_at: time-range queries for audit reports; action: filter by action type (CREATE, UPDATE, DELETE, APPROVE, REJECT)

methods: findOverlapping(employeeId: string, startDate: Date, endDate: Date): Promise<LeaveRequest[]>
updateStatus(id: string, status: LeaveStatus, approvedBy?: string, approvedAt?: Date): Promise<LeaveRequest>
findByEmployeeIdAndPolicyId(employeeId: string, policyId: string, fiscalYear: number): Promise<LeaveBalance | null>

data_notes: Persistence design for the leave management module. Six conceptual tables defined: employees, leave_types, leave_policies, leave_requests, leave_balances, audit_logs. Six repository interfaces with concrete Pg* implementations backed by PostgreSQL via pg Pool. All tables follow the existing domain model from DOMAIN.md. Index rationale reflects access patterns: employee lookups, status filtering for manager approval queues, date-range queries for calendar/overlap detection, fiscal-year filtering for balance accrual cycles, and entity-type/entity-id composite lookups for audit trails. The audit_logs table satisfies GP-002 (all state-changing operations write an audit record). FK relationships link leave_requests to employees (employee + approver), leave_types, and leave_balances to employees and leave_policies.
